title: Fatty acid enrichment in metalimnetic zooplankton: implications for trophic transfer in a stratified lake
content:
Abstract
This study aimed to compare the fatty acids (FA) compositions and stoichiometry of zooplankton between the epilimnion and metalimnion of a stratified meso-eutrophic lake. We observed substantial differences in the contents of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) and monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA) between the two layers, with metalimnetic zooplankton exhibiting two to three times higher contents of PUFA (C18:2 n-6, C18:3 n-3, C20:5 n-3, C22:6 n-3) and MUFA (C16:1 n-7, C17:1 n-7, C18:1 n-9 (cis), C20:1 n-9, C22:1 n-9) than epilimnetic zooplankton. While small discrepancies in zooplankton community structure were observed between the strata, they alone could not explain the considerable disparity in PUFA and MUFA contents. We propose that the elevated FA contents in the metalimnion were associated with the larger zooplankton body size, the higher proportion of egg-bearing females, and potentially with better food quality in this layer. The high PUFA and MUFA contents in metalimnetic zooplankton enhanced their nutritional value for fish, potentially improving fish growth and health. However, carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus contents did not differ significantly, indicating stoichiometric homeostasis of the zooplankton. These findings improve our understanding of trophic interactions in stratified lakes and may have implications for fisheries and aquaculture management.
